headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error from a broad-network support agent paired with a local game-playing agent that has no shared workspace or direct ingestion path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and oh-my-openagent. A has no io_surfaces and no network egress; B uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks, but nothing shows it ingests A’s outputs by default. The pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe A’s text into B’s tool prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B touches project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and provider auth data and has broad network egress. In a pair, leakage risk exists if B is pointed at sensitive local artifacts from A’s environment; the shared workspace is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are run in the same workspace containing secrets or project code, B can transmit those contents off-host.
IF B is granted access to provider auth data or session history from A’s environment, exfiltration risk increases.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before starting B.
Restrict B’s network egress to approved domains.
Rotate any provider auth data exposed to B.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write, network, or concurrency surfaces, so it cannot materially conflict with B on shared mutable resources from the profiles alone. B can write to several config and cache paths and supports multiple instances, but without a shared writable target with A the overlap is limited and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same config or cache directory, write conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator maps A and B onto the same mutable git or filesystem state, contention increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct config directories.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo.
Use file locks for any shared mutable path.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has tool-use and action surfaces (team_send_message, team_task_create, LSP actions) that can operationalize A’s outputs if they are forwarded without verification. A is a game-playing agent with no documented safeguards against being treated as authoritative, so the pair can cascade errors in default integration patterns, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s generated text or facts without a verification step, incorrect outputs can be acted on.
IF A is used as a source for code edits or team messages, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B acts.
Require B to cite source evidence before tool use.
Limit B to read-only mode during evaluation.
Log A-to-B handoffs for audit.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A’s outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles provider auth prompts, installation identifiers, session history, and project code, while A is open-source game-playing with no data classes touched. The pair creates a compliance mismatch if regulated or secret-bearing data from B’s environment is exposed to A’s less constrained context, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF B processes regulated data such as customer code or auth prompts in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, compliance review is required.
IF session history or provider auth data is retained beyond policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B’s workspace.
Shorten retention on session history.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment.
Mask auth prompts in logs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
